## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D Pokémon-inspired game with combat based on Friday Night Funkin’-style rhythm notes.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport no wider than 1280px) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created an original, single-file browser game called “Wildbeat” with original creature names and hand-drawn canvas art.
- Implemented exploration, random creature encounters, and arrow-key rhythm duels.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable game in `index.html`, including title screen, trail exploration, creature battles, rhythm note timing, health/level progression, touch controls, and sound toggle.
- Ran JavaScript syntax check successfully.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved screenshots of the title, world, and battle views.

### Active
- Validate screenshot/gameplay behavior and address any bugs found.

### Blocked
- Browser check reported favicon 404; not game-breaking.
- No battle screenshot was inspected after the final capture; the latest inspected screenshot was `screenshots/wildbeat-world.jpg` earlier in the run.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/wildbeat-battle.jpg` and confirm the battle view renders correctly.
2. Test rhythm input and battle completion in the browser; fix any issues.
3. Check `git status` and report final implementation and testing status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/wildbeat-battle.jpg`: Latest battle screenshot, captured but not inspected.
- `screenshots/wildbeat-world.jpg`: Previously inspected world screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local HTTP server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- `playwright-cli` is installed and the Chromium browser was installed for testing.

  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs

  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
